summary: Fire Safety in Space is an interactive, Super Intelligence (SI)-powered web dashboard built on NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data (22 experimental tables, 2,009 tests). Designed for the Flame in Freefall challenge, it solves the problem of fragmented, hard-to-compare PSI CSV schemas by normalizing oxygen concentrations, mapping parameter coverage gaps across 9 categories, comparing 2–3 investigations side-by-side, and ranking series for lunar habitats (>=30% O2, <=10.2 psi), predictive modeling, suppression (CO2/He), and smoke detection. An integrated tool-grounded SI Research Agent (GPT-6 Luna via Coarena API) inspects raw PSI records on demand with live reasoning traces and strict citations, turning complex ISS combustion data into clear, actionable insights for safer Moon bases, Mars missions, and terrestrial fire safety.
details:
Fire Safety in Space is an open-source, SI-powered web explorer that summarizes, compares, and ranks 22 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion investigations (2,009 experimental test rows) for human spaceflight and terrestrial fire-safety applications.

How It Works: The FastAPI backend (backend/psi_data.py) loads experimental_dataset.json, cleans stray BOM characters, excludes O2 flow rates (mg/s, sccm), normalizes oxygen fractions vs percentages with transparent unit-assumption notes, evaluates parameter coverage across 9 categories (O2, pressure, airflow, fuel/material, sample/burner size, diluents N2/He/CO2, temperature, combustion result, cameras/sensors), and computes weighted relevance rankings for four exploration scenarios: Lunar base (>=30% O2), Predictive modeling, Fire suppression & dilution, and Smoke/aerosol detection.

User Experience & Visualizations: The React + TypeScript + Tailwind UI provides sidebar filters (series name, O2 presence, >=30% lunar O2 threshold, minimum test count), a Recharts oxygen range chart with Earth (21% O2 / 14.7 psi) and Moon (30%+ O2 / <=10.2 psi) reference lines, an interactive Gap Map with formula-safe CSV and Excel (.xlsx) export, a 2-3 series side-by-side schema diff highlighting differences, a 22-series catalog, and a raw test inspector with per-column completeness.

Tool-Grounded SI Research Agent: Powered by Coarena Model API (GPT-6 Luna) over Server-Sent Events (SSE), the agent uses three live retrieval tools (list_psi_series, inspect_psi_table, search_psi_records) to inspect actual CSV rows, numeric bounds, and categorical fuels on demand. It streams its reasoning trace and tool calls, always cites exact series names, PSI accession numbers (PSI-10 to PSI-159), and source CSV filenames, separates PSI data from challenge context to prevent prompt injection, and explicitly discloses that PSI currently lacks Moon (0.16g) and Mars (0.38g) partial-gravity tests (expected from LUCI and FM2).

Technology Stack & Hardware Context: Python 3.13, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pandas, OpenPyXL, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Anthropic-compatible Coarena API (GPT-6 Luna), and Docker (live at https://nasa.rell.tech/). Domain metadata maps CIR/ACME (BRE, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame, CFI-G), CIR/MDCA (FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI), and MSG/ISS Aerosol hardware (BASS, BASS-II, SPICE, SLICE, SAFFIRE-1/-2/-3, SAME/-R, DAFT), plus Earth spin-offs such as ISS fine-water-mist extinguishers, smoke detectors, and firefighter gear.

Team Blum Contributions: ifritov — repository initialization, NASA PSI dataset curation and schema unification (experimental_dataset.json); maxim-paradise — FastAPI data pipeline, tool-grounded SSE SI agent, React integration, and Docker deployment; Oleksandra Nedielko (Aleksa) — UI/UX design, visual system, initial Streamlit prototype, and documentation.
